abstract: We consider two-player zero-sum concurrent stochastic games played over a finite state space for an infinite number of stages. In every stage, both players simultaneously and independently choose an action. Then, given the current state and chosen actions, the successor state is selected according to a stochastic transition function. We consider limit-average objectives, where Player 1 maximizes the long-run average of rewards assigned to every transition. The value from an initial state is the maximal expectation that Player 1 can ensure. We study the two basic computational problems: (a) the approximation problem of computing the values within an arbitrary additive error, and (b) the exact problem of deciding whether the value at a state is at least a given threshold. The previous results in the literature establish: (a) the approximation problem belongs to TFNP[NP], and (b) the exact problem belongs to PSPACE, via the theory of the reals, and is SQRT-SUM-hard. Our contributions are as follows. (a) Our main result shows that the approximation problem is in TFNP, and that the associated gap or promise problem is in NP $\cap$ coNP. (b) We also show that the exact problem is in $\exists\mathbb{R} \cap \text{co-}\exists\mathbb{R}$, i.e., it reduces to both the existential and the universal theory of the reals, and that it is PosSLP-hard.
